description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.

There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. See the Drug Interactions Thesaurus.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.

There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of treatment with an angiotensin II antagonist. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. See the Drug Interactions Thesaurus.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

mecanisme_en: In the indications where this combination is possible, there is an increased risk of deterioration of renal function, or even acute renal failure, and an increase in hyperkalemia, as well as hypotension and syncope.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of treatment with an angiotensin II antagonist. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. See the Drug Interactions Thesaurus.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use: Hydrate the patient and monitor renal function at the start of treatment and regularly during the combination.

These effects are generally reversible. Furthermore, there may be a reduction in the antihypertensive effect.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of treatment with an angiotensin II antagonist. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of treatment with an angiotensin II antagonist. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. See the Drug Interactions Thesaurus.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of treatment with an angiotensin II antagonist. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. See the Drug Interactions Thesaurus.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of treatment with an angiotensin II antagonist. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. See the Drug Interactions Thesaurus.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

Monitoring is necessary, particularly of bleeding time.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of treatment with an angiotensin II antagonist. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. See the Drug Interactions Thesaurus.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: It is important to consider the risk associated with combining a drug with atropinic effects (imipramine, phenothiazine neuroleptics, antispasmodics, certain H1 antihistamines, etc.) in a patient treated with an anticholinesterase. Besides the possible reduction in the therapeutic effect of the latter, abrupt discontinuation of atropinic treatment exposes the patient to the risk of uncovering the muscarinic effects of the parasympathomimetic, with symptoms resembling a cholinergic crisis, which may manifest as seizures.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of treatment with an angiotensin II antagonist. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an angiotensin II antagonist in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion. See the Drug Interactions Thesaurus.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the angiotensin II antagonist, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of angiotensin II antagonist and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of treatment with an angiotensin II antagonist. description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.
mecanisme_en: In congestive heart failure treated with diuretics, start with a very low dose of ACE inhibitor, possibly after reducing the dose of the concomitant potassium-depleting diuretic. In all cases: monitor renal function (serum creatinine) during the first few weeks of ACE inhibitor treatment. There is a risk of sudden hypotension and/or acute renal failure when initiating or increasing the dosage of an ACE inhibitor in patients with pre-existing sodium and water depletion.

description_interaction_en: Precaution for use In arterial hypertension, when prior diuretic treatment may have caused sodium and water depletion, it is necessary to: - either stop the diuretic before starting treatment with the ACE inhibitor, and reintroduce a hypokalemic diuretic if necessary later; - or administer reduced initial doses of ACE inhibitor and gradually increase the dosage.

description_interaction_en: It is important to consider the risk associated with combining a drug with atropinic effects (imipramine, phenothiazine neuroleptics, antispasmodics, certain H1 antihistamines, etc.) in a patient treated with an anticholinesterase. Besides the possible reduction in the therapeutic effect of the latter, abrupt discontinuation of atropinic treatment exposes the patient to the risk of uncovering the muscarinic effects of the parasympathomimetic, with symptoms resembling a cholinergic crisis, which may manifest as seizures.

description_interaction_en: It is important to consider the risk associated with combining a drug with atropinic effects (imipramine, phenothiazine neuroleptics, antispasmodics, certain H1 antihistamines, etc.) in a patient treated with an anticholinesterase. Besides the possible reduction in the therapeutic effect of the latter, abrupt discontinuation of atropinic treatment exposes the patient to the risk of uncovering the muscarinic effects of the parasympathomimetic, with symptoms resembling a cholinergic crisis, which may manifest as seizures.
